News.title: The parasite behind an ‘explosive diarrhoea’ outbreak in the US
News.content:
Cyclospora is a parasite that is found in human faeces.

Tiny parasitic eggs, called oocysts, are released through human poo. They need about one to two weeks outside the body to mature and become able to infect someone else.

Usually, this is not a problem because sewage systems safely remove human waste and stop the parasite from spreading to other people.

But if sewage leaks or treatment systems fail, tiny traces of human faeces can get into water supplies.

If crops are then grown, watered, or washed with this contaminated water, Cyclospora can end up on food – and make people sick.

The parasite is most common in warm, humid places, where the conditions help it survive and multiply.

Britain records only a small handful of cases every year, almost exclusively in travellers who have returned from the tropics. In 2015, the UK reported 79 cases in a single summer that were associated with holidaymakers returning from Mexico.

Previous outbreaks in the US have been linked to food that’s been grown in tropical climates, mostly in South and Central America, and then imported into the country, but it has also been detected during the summer months in warmer states like Florida and California.

A small 2022 Florida outbreak was linked in part to bagged lettuce in a Caesar salad kit.

The current outbreak has been traced back to a single supplier of iceberg lettuce grown in Mexico, used in the Taco Bell locations where sick people ate.

Part of the problem is that in a modern food system, when food is grown and processed on a massive, industrialised scale and shipped thousands of miles, a single contaminated irrigation source can infect countless people.

How do people catch it?

People become infected when they consume food or water contaminated with human faeces containing Cyclospora.

It can’t spread person-to-person like Covid-19 or the flu, and it usually takes between one and two weeks before symptoms show.

Fresh fruits and vegetables are the most common sources, partly because they absorb large amounts of water while growing and partly because they are often eaten raw. High cooking temperatures kill the parasite, reducing the risk of infection.

After investigating dozens of options, the current outbreak has been traced back to fresh lettuce supplied to Taco Bell. The chain had earlier removed not only its lettuce but its coriander, and guacamole from its menu.

Cyclospora is notoriously difficult to trace, and the investigation has taken weeks.

As opposed to a bacteria or a virus, parasites have complex life cycles and can quickly transition through multiple microscopic forms, making them evasive to traditional lab testing procedures.

Recent funding cuts under Donald Trump have also made surveillance much more challenging, say experts.

In July last year, the Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network (FoodNet), an agency within the CDC, stopped tracking six of eight food-borne pathogens, including cyclospora, owing to significant cuts to its budget.

The CDC is said to now be faced with a shortage of vital resources, including equipment and personnel, required to tackle the outbreak.

Where is it spreading?

At least 34 US states have reported cases of cyclosporiasis since May 1.

Michigan is the hardest-hit state, with more than 3,300 of the roughly 7,000 confirmed and suspected cases recorded nationwide so far.

The state typically reports only around 50 cases a year.

The Midwest appears to be the epicentre, with Ohio, West Virginia, and Kentucky also seeing significant increases and investigators have linked illnesses in these states to Taco Bell locations that served shredded iceberg lettuce from the Mexico supplier.

However, several other states, including New York, Tennessee, California, and Florida, have also reported a rise in infections.

Cyclosporiasis cases usually increase during the summer months in the US, as warmer temperatures help the parasite survive. But the CDC is investigating whether the Midwest outbreak is connected to the wider rise in cases across the country.

New York state officials, for example, said they had recorded twice as many cases between January and June this year compared with the same period last year.

What are the symptoms?

The main symptoms of cyclosporiasis is frequent, sudden, sometimes explosive diarrhoea, typically beginning between one and two weeks after infection.

Other symptoms include abdominal cramping, nausea, unintended weight loss, and extreme tiredness.

Young children, people over 60, and those with weakened immune systems – for example, people undergoing chemotherapy or living with HIV – are more susceptible to severe illness.

Deaths are exceedingly rare, and there is effective treatment available with a course of a prescription drug called trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

Without it, the parasitic infection can last as long as a month, although many cases do clear up on their own.

How can you avoid catching it?

Past outbreaks of cyclospora have been linked to batches of fruit and vegetables grown or irrigated in dirty water – historically, items like raspberries, basil, coriander, and salad leaves.

US health officials have now advised customers not to eat shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia.

They say the public don’t need to avoid any other foods.

The CDC says that thorough washing of fruits and vegetables under clean, running water is the best way to avoid Cyclospora – even if produce is labelled as “pre-washed.”

Cooking food at 70 degrees or higher also effectively kills the bug.

Washing your hands with soap and water before and after handling fresh fruit and vegetables is also critical to eliminate the risk of cross-contamination between different foodstuffs, the agency advises.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: US aid workers move into controversial new Ebola quarantine centre in Kenya
News.content:
Seven ‌American aid workers have been moved into a controversial new Ebola quarantine centre in Kenya, despite a judge ordering a halt after widespread public opposition.

The head of a United States charity told Reuters its workers were undergoing three weeks’ isolation at the high-security field hospital set up in a Kenyan air base.

The US State Department confirmed that a group of asymptomatic Americans who had been working on the international response to Congo’s latest Ebola outbreak had “voluntarily moved ⁠to the Kenya facility for precautionary monitoring and isolation”.

Soon after the outbreak was declared in mid-May in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), America announced it would build a quarantine centre for returning US aid workers to isolate in Kenya, before they were allowed back into the US.

Donald Trump vowed his administration “cannot and will not allow” any cases of Ebola to enter the United States.

The scheme triggered outcry in Kenya, with opponents claiming Nairobi was trading sovereignty for US aid, and putting the population at risk from the deadly haemorrhagic fever.

A local court suspended work on the project pending a legal challenge and later found the health minister in contempt when preparations proceeded.

However, work on the facility has reportedly continued.

Sports.title: World Cup star who outshone Argentina and Spain ‘receives stunning transfer offer despite Lionel Messi interest’
Sports.content:
CAPE Verde’s Vozinha has been tipped for a move to Chilean giants on a free transfer.

Colo Colo are in talks to sign the World Cup sensation, according to Fabrizio Romano.



Reports suggest that an initial offer has been sent and Vozinha’s camp have provided a counter proposal.

The Liga de Primera champions are set to pick between the Cape Verdean and Uruguayan international and Monterrey keeper Santiago Mele soon.



But this is not the only deal on the table for the 40-year-old as several clubs remain interested globally.

A report from AS in Spain insisted that David Beckham is a massive fan of the goalkeeper after watching him against Argentina in the last 32.

So, Vozinha could also be set for a move to Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami.

Speaking on finding a new club, the former bus driver revealed: “It’s one of the first things I want to sort out. I love soccer.

“Being here, at 40 years old, is because I truly have this passion.

“I want to play for at least another year or two, or see how long my body can take it; we never know what tomorrow will bring.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“I want to play, and I hope to find a team that really wants me as a player, not as a marketing person.”

But wherever Vozinha goes next is going to draw the eyes of the world, especially as he now boasts 29.4million Instagram followers.

The shot-stopper made four appearances at the 2026 World Cup making 4.50 saves per game with two clean sheets.

His performance made the headlines after his box office performance against Spain, where he helped hold the finalists to a goalless draw.

Uruguay provided another blockbuster clash before they took holders Argentina into the depths of extra time.



He was handed the Player of the Match award for keeping a clean sheet against Spain.

And many claimed he was robbed of the same award against Argentina.

Expectedly, it was awarded to Messi.



But his fame has not been stunted by Cape Verde’s tournament exit with a species of sea slug even being named after him.

Vozinha – whose real name is Josimar Dias – departed from Liga Portugal 2 side Chaves before their World Cup campaign.

Last season, he only made 19 appearances in Portugal as he managed six clean sheets and 2.32 saves per game.

With 19 years of professional football behind him and 280 appearances, the journeyman has played across Cape Verde, Angola, Moldova, Cyprus, Slovakia, and Portugal.

Sports.title: Hannah Hampton stuns in one-piece swimsuit as England Lionesses hero chills out on summer holiday
Sports.content:
LIONESSES star Hannah Hampton left fans stunned in a one-piece swimsuit during a recent holiday.

The goalkeeper, 25, has become a huge star after she helped England retain their European Championship title last year.



The Chelsea shot-stopper has been taking some time off after the Women’s Super League finished with a well-deserved trip to Zanzibar.

Hampton uploaded a set of photos giving fans a glimpse into her luxury trip as she dazzled in a black swimsuit while sitting outside of the Salaam Cave.





She was seen sitting on a rock while petting a turtle as she decided to unwind before the start of pre-season.

Hampton wrote a caption in Swahili that translated to: “Peace and tranquility”.

She also shared some snaps of herself enjoying a safari and an impressive painting of a lion.

Hampton also made sure she represented by donning her England goalkeeping jersey, as well as an elegant low-cut yellow top that showed off her tanlines.



Fans were blown away by her incredible display as they took to the comments.

One wrote: “This looks so good it must be ai.”

Another said: “She’s a fine keeper.”



A third added: “Very beautiful and cute.”

And a fourth chimed in: “Hannah is a natural beauty and a top keeper.”

Earlier this month Hampton also stunned in a yellow dress during a night out during her holiday.

She often posts glamorous pictures for her 405,000 Instagram followers.

Hampton was also seen paying a visit to Wimbledon during her break from the game.



She has made 79 appearances for Chelsea since joining from Aston Villa in 2023 – winning two WSL titles and the FA Cup.

And the rising star has also picked up 29 England caps after taking over the No 1 shirt from Mary Earps.

Sports.title: World Cup final will see Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal face off for first time ever 19 years after viral baby pic
Sports.content:
SOME stories are simply too unbelievable to make up.

Nineteen years ago, a fresh-faced Lionel Messi cradled and bathed a six-month-old baby during a charity photoshoot for a Barcelona and UNICEF calendar.



On Sunday night at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, that same baby – Lamine Yamal – will walk out opposite his childhood idol as Spain and Argentina battle for the biggest prize in football.

It will be the first time the pair have ever shared the same pitch competitively.



Messi said on Friday: “That picture with Lamine, it’s something crazy. Life is full of surprises.

“Now we are facing each other in a final after a photo was taken of us when he was a baby, it’s just insane.”



If there was ever a World Cup final that felt written by Hollywood, this is it.

The famous photographs have become some of the sport’s most iconic images.

They came about after a Catalan newspaper held a raffle to find babies to feature alongside Barcelona players in a UNICEF charity calendar shoot.

Yamal, then just six months old, was one of only 12 children selected.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

By pure chance – or perhaps fate – he was paired with Messi, who was only 20-years-old himself and still at the beginning of a career that would change football forever.

Back then, nobody could have imagined the smiling infant in Messi’s arms would one day become the player tipped to inherit his crown.

Yet there is an eerie symmetry to everything that has followed.



Both burst onto the scene as fearless left-footed forwards cutting in from the right-wing, gliding past defenders with the same balance, close control and unmatched confidence.

It has even prompted fans to joke that Messi somehow passed on his magic during that charity photoshoot nearly two decades ago.

The numbers make the comparison even more remarkable.

Messi had scored just 11 senior goals and won one La Liga title and one Champions League by the time he celebrated his 19th birthday.

Yamal, who only turned 19 on Monday, has already netted 56 career goals, lifted three La Liga titles, won the Copa del Rey, and helped Spain lift Euro 2024 when he was just 16.



MASTER VS APPRENTICE

For all the inevitable comparisons, Sunday feels less like a battle between equals and more like a symbolic passing of the torch.

Messi arrives in New Jersey chasing history one last time as Argentina look to become the first team since Brazil in 1962 to defend what Fifa President Gianni Infantino once called “the most iconic, the most beautiful, the most incredible trophy in the world.”

The Argentina captain already owns one World Cup winner’s medal, eight Ballon d’Or awards and countless other honours.



Now, at 39, he stands on the brink of leading Argentina to a fourth World Cup title and strengthening his case for a remarkable NINTH Ballon d’Or.

The Inter Miami megastar has been the outstanding player of the World Cup, scoring eight goals to sit level with Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race and looking well placed to win a third World Cup Golden Ball – awarded to the tournament’s best player.

Yamal’s tournament has been very different.

The teenager has scored only once against Saudi Arabia, but has been one of the driving forces behind a Spain side built on collective brilliance rather than individual statistics.

His influence stretches far beyond goals.



DEJA VU

Just as Messi once inspired Barcelona’s golden generation, Yamal has become the face of a new era built around La Masia.

The parallels between club and country are striking.

Before Spain conquered the world in 2010, Barcelona had just won back-to-back league titles under Pep Guardiola with a squad built around academy graduates including Messi, Xavi, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Busquets, Gerard Pique and Carles Puyol.



Spain’s World Cup-winning squad that summer featured seven Barcelona players and eight La Masia graduates.

It could well have been nine. The authorities in Spain did everything to try and get Messi to represent La Roja having acquired Spanish citizenship in 2005, but instead he wanted to play for his beloved Argentina.

Fast forward to 2026 and history seems to be repeating itself.

Barcelona have again won successive league titles, this time under Hansi Flick, while Spain’s squad contains eight Barcelona players and eight products of La Masia.

Yamal is now the leading light of a new generation featuring the likes of Pau Cubarsi, Gavi and Dani Olmo, who echo the core that dominated world football in the late 2000s and early 2010s.



There are even more curious links.

Spain beat the Netherlands to win their only World Cup on July 11, 2010 – just two days before Yamal celebrated his third birthday.

At that point Messi was already regarded as the world’s finest player and would later collect the second of his eight Ballon d’Or trophies.

Now, the two nations meet again with everything on the line.

EUROPE’S BEST VS SOUTH AMERICA’S BEST

They were actually supposed to face each other in the Finalissima in Qatar in March before the fixture was abandoned because of security concerns surrounding conflict in the Middle East.



Instead, football has delivered something even bigger.

Spain arrive unbeaten in 37 matches, excluding penalty shootout defeats.

Argentina are chasing another chapter in an extraordinary dynasty after winning the Copa America in 2021 and 2024, the Finalissima in 2022 and the World Cup later that same year.

Throughout that chapter, the core of the squad is the same – led by the numinous figure of Messi.

For Yamal, it is another chance to measure himself against greatness.



Last year he faced Cristiano Ronaldo in the Nations League final, where the Portuguese icon scored in a 2-2 draw before Portugal prevailed on penalties.

Now comes another generational showdown against the player so many believe is the greatest of all-time.

FULL CIRCLE MOMENT

It is funny how football has a habit of coming full circle, but this is on a different level.

It was 18-and-a-half years ago when Messi gently held a baby in his arms for a charity calendar.

On Sunday, just days after turning 19, that same child will walk out beside him before trying to stop his idol lifting another World Cup.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Messi was 20 when that unforgettable photograph was taken.

Now, with almost exactly 20 years between them, football’s generational talents will finally collide on the grandest stage of them all.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland turns heads in ‘blouse’ outfit and bottoms as he parties with girlfriend following World Cup heroics
Sports.content:
AFTER a strong World Cup for Norway, Erling Haaland is quite rightly enjoying himself.

The Man City striker, who scored 61 goals for club and country last season, became a sensation in America during the World Cup and he has gained 30 million followers on Instagram as a result.



The 25-year-old has been partying in Italy with his girlfriend – fellow Norwegian Isabel Haugseng Johansen – and he has been turning heads with his attire.

Wearing what can only be described as a ‘blouse’ outfit and pyjama bottoms, the man certainly has his own style.



Fans are loving the goal machine’s personality online and fans rushed to the comments section.

One user said: “I wana be so rich that I can go clubbing in pyjamas.”

A second posted: “You are very lucky that you are super rich so I really can’t say much…”

A third commented: “Bro is scoring off the pitch just as easily as he scores on it. Living his best life!”

A fourth wrote: “Haaland is living his best life at this point, doesn’t even care about what is happening in the World cup anymore.”

Norway went out to England in the quarter-finals, but that didn’t stop Haaland from going out and partying in Miami.



Plenty of Haaland memes have been storming the internet since Norway got knocked out, too, with his head being put on the end of a mop and his neck extending across elevator doors, to name a couple.

Haaland is quite rightly enjoying his break before he has to return to Man City and prepare for the new season.

This time, he’ll be doing so under Enzo Maresca, the man who has been enlisted to replace the legendary Pep Guardiola.

Sports.title: ‘I think I’ve pulled my thigh’ – Wayne Rooney injures himself doing Viking row as forfeit for wrong World Cup prediction
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY’S debt to Norway’s Erling Haaland has been repaid after he bet against the Scandinavians making the quarter finals.

With an England flag at the helm and Micah Richards with a drum, Rooney took to the Hudson River after his World Cup punt went wrong.



On BBC Sport, Rooney previously promised: “If Norway get to the quarter finals, I’ll go on the River Mersey and I’ll row down it.”

Norway exceeded all expectations in North America – beating Iraq, Senegal, and Ivory Coast.





Then they shocked the world, overcoming five-time world champions Brazil in a box office 2-1 last 16 victory.

Talisman Erling Haaland bagged a brace to stun the South Americans and called Rooney out.

The Man City ace said: “Wayney boy, Wayne Rooney…

“I expect you to go out on a rowing trip.”



The challenge comes from the viral Norway celebration where players and fans perform a synchronised row to the beat of a drum while shouting “Ro. Ro. Ro”.

Post-match on live TV, Rooney admitted: “Yeah, I’m a man of my word. It might have to be the Hudson River when we’re in New York.”

Joe Hart was quick to chime in, adding that he would row with him.

Taking to the famous river on Friday, Rooney spoke down the camera: “Haaland, as promised we are doing our row in the Hudson River.”

To chants of “Rooney, Rooney, Rooney”, the Manchester United star shyly admitted: “I think I’ve pulled my thigh!”



Richards joined the crew with his makeshift drum as he ordered Rooney to listen to instructions.

Sports.title: Fallen Bundesliga champions banned from using OWN CREST and revert to badge from over 100 years ago in bitter legal row
Sports.content:
1860 MUNICH have temporarily lost the rights to their iconic crest amid the club’s ongoing crisis that led to relegation to the fourth division.

Munich are one of the most historic German clubs and one of the key founders of the Bundesliga in 1963 that won the title in 1966 as well as the Cup in 1942 and 1964.



However, the Lions have endured a dramatic fall from grace and it all started in 2004 when they were relegated from the top flight – they have since never returned.

Munich have since found themselves lost in the wilderness as they spent 13 years in the second division and another eight in the third tier until their drop to the fourth category last season.



Now the once German giants have found themselves embroiled in a bitter legal row that doesn’t allow them to wear their own badge until further notice.

According to Bulinews, the sudden change comes down to the merchandising rights that are still held by investor Hasan Ismaik’s company.

Although Ismaik’s company still holds the rights to the name and logo, it is not permitted for commercial use purposes.

Therefore, Munich had to find a solution and looked back at previous badges before landing on the most recent crest they wore before their suspended lion emblem.

After some in-depth research, club chiefs announced the team will don an insignia they used over 100 years ago.

Munich released the following statement: “Until the lion can once again be used without restrictions as the crest, the new operating company will temporarily use the historical FA crest.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“As soon as the legal requirements are met, the lion will once again be used as the crest of TSV 1860 Munich.

“In recent days, we have been frequently asked about the origin and meaning of the FA crest.

“Therefore, we have asked the club history department for a historical overview.

“According to research by Claus Melchior (club history department), the FA crest was first documented in 1919.

“However, no definitive information about its exact origins is available to date.



“Historical commemorative publications and team photos show that the lion has been the defining crest of the TSV 1860 Munich footballers since before the First World War.

“The FA crest is part of the history of our football department and is therefore being used during the current transition phase.”

Sports.title: What kit are England wearing against France?
Sports.content:
DESPITE the heartbreak England suffered against Argentina on Wednesday, the Three Lions still have one more game to play at the World Cup!

It comes against France in the third-place play-off, with the winner earning a bronze medal at the tournament.



Thomas Tuchel‘s side suffered a devastating loss as their bitter rivals scored two late goals to end England’s dream of bringing football home once again.

Tonight’s game comes amid reports of fractures in the Three Lions’ camp, with reports of players being unhappy with the defensive tactics Tuchel employed when they were 1-0 up.



The German boss has faced plenty of criticism since the loss, most notably from US President Donald Trump, who blasted Tuchel for making Harry Kane a “defensive player”.

However, they must forget that if they want to beat Les Bleus in Miami, who will be wanting to give legendary manager Didier Deschamps the best possible send off.



Deschamps is leaving his role as France manager after 14 years in charge, leading them to glory at the 2018 World Cup, before losing on penalties in the final four years ago.

While Les Bleus will also be disappointed to not be in the final, superstar Kylian Mbappe is still chasing a second Golden Boot – the Real Madrid star is currently tied with Lionel Messi on eight goals.

What kit are England wearing against France?

Despite technically being the away team according to Fifa tonight, England will still line up in their home kit.

This is because France are wearing their all-blue strip, leaving the Three Lions free to also wear their home kit.



This will be the sixth time that Harry Kane and Co have worn the white kit, which they also wore in the loss to Argentina.

The only time they wore their away red kit was in the 2-0 over Panama in the final game of the group stages.

Sports.title: ‘I got a little insight…’ – Souness reveals Dubai moment that hints at why Cole Palmer didn’t make England squad
Sports.content:
GRAEME SOUNESS has revealed Cole Palmer gave him an “insight” into his character after seeing him act “extremely rude” to someone in a Dubai restaurant.

The former Liverpool boss was asked about Thomas Tuchel‘s controversial decision to leave the Chelsea midfielder out of his final World Cup squad.



England‘s disastrous World Cup exit against Argentina in the semi-finals has opened up the debate about his omission again after Tuchel parked the bus in Atlanta.

In May, Tuchel explained he left Palmer at home because his record with England was “not outstanding enough” to make him an automatic pick.



Palmer’s exclusion was a head-scratcher for some fans even though he didn’t have the best individual season for the Blues.

But Souness has hinted there may be another reason why Palmer didn’t make the cut after an encounter in Dubai.

He told World Cup Uncensored with Simon Jordan: “I think he’s outstanding [as a player].

“I don’t know what his character is, I got a little insight into that in Dubai in February where he was extremely rude to someone in a restaurant.”

Souness also took issue with two England stars who went to the World Cup in Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson.

The Scot said there “wasn’t enough football in them” and branded Arsenal star Rice “limited” compared to the likes of Spain’s Rodri.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

He continued: “I don’t see enough football in the two of them [Rice and Anderson]. I don’t see them hurting anyone.

“Declan Rice, for me, limited. You hear people talk about Declan Rice, ‘a world-class footballer’, I think he might be a centre-half.

“My take on being a central midfield player is – if you’re a striker, or you’re someone in wide areas, they want me to have the minimum touch. Ideally one touch or two touch.

“People say about midfielders ‘he carries the ball really well’. You don’t want to carry the ball really well!



“I’ve got Declan Rice running with the ball, runs 20 yards, confronted by an opposition player, handbrake goes on, passes it square.”

On the night, Tuchel claimed England were “too passive” despite converting to a back five in the last 15 minutes of the game.

He has copped plenty of flak for his negative tactics that saw him take off goalscorer Anthony Gordon and replace him with defender Ezri Konsa.

But he accepted full responsibility for England’s agonising exit amid huge pressure on his position.

The German said: “I take responsibility. If it’s easier, if someone takes the blame, I take the blame. It’s not a problem.



“If this is the deal that you 

“That’s just how it is, and we have to live with this. So it’s our pain, my pain, and the players’ pain.

Sports.title: 'Celebrate our World Cup victory, England's immigrant squad uniting us'
Sports.content:
'Celebrate our World Cup victory, England's immigrant squad uniting us'

Rather than feeling depressed at England’s exit from the World Cup, fans should remember how proud the team, with players of mostly foreign descent, made us, says Brian Reade

View 2 Images England squad kicked toxic lies into touch (Image: Phil Duncan/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Are you looking forward to watching England play for World Cup glory tonight? What do you mean, they were knocked out on Wednesday? They’re still in it. OK it’s not the final, and the chances are if the real France turn up for tonight’s third-place play-off they’ll finish fourth, but at least they made it to the final weekend, unlike Brazil, Germany and, erm, Scotland.

‌



Still not looking on the bright side of life? Come on, you won’t have to hear that nonsensical soundbite “it’s coming home” until at least the 2028 Euros and besides, who wanted to win the most corrupt World Cup in history thanks to the vile Infantino/Trump love-in?

‌



Plus, tomorrow night when the final is on, if you go to the pub you won’t be soaked by attention-seeking, once-every-two-year fans throwing their lager in the air when a goal is scored. Or, if you stay in you can watch Antiques Roadshow on BBC2 instead of torturing your ears by listening to banal cliches from co-commentator zombies like Lee Dixon.

‌



Rather than feeling depressed at England’s latest painful exit from a major tournament, fans should remember how proud those footballers made them feel this summer. How they thrilled with their skills and offered hope by proving England are not that far behind the best in the world.

View 2 Images England's footballers of mostly foreign descent have united England. (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



But most importantly, at a time when political grifters fool millions of ordinary Brits into believing that their biggest problem is immigrants making them poorer, those footballers offered a sound rebuttal. Here’s why. Of the 26-man England squad, 18 either come from abroad or have parents from outside Britain. Marc Guehi was born in the Ivory Coast and moved here when he was one, while Trevor Chalobah was born in Sierra Leone and came here when he was two. Harry Kane’s dad is from Ireland, Jude Bellingham is Irish through his father and Jamaican through his mother and Declan Rice is so Irish he played for them three times.

Ezri Konsa has a Congolese father and an Angolan mother and Jarell Quansah has a Ghanaian father. Nico O’Reilly, Morgan Rogers, Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins all have a parent of Jamaican descent. Reece James’s father is a Grenadian-Dominican, Djed Spence is of Jamaican and Kenyan descent, and Kobbie Mainoo’s parents are from Ghana. Bukayo Saka’s parents are Nigerian, Marcus Rashford’s father is Jamaican and Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have Nigerian parents. All of those players are eligible to play for other nations but they chose England.

Had Reform’s UK Deportation Command (which aims to remove up to 288,000 immigrants every year) or Restore’s planned mass deportations of two million foreigners been in place over the past couple of decades, how many of those players would be here today to give England a fighting chance of glory?

Article continues below

Before anyone swallows the lie about immigrants making them worse off they should reflect not just on how they would get treated in hospitals or care homes without foreign-born workers, but how much poorer this country’s talent pool and culture would be. This summer these footballers of mostly foreign descent have united England and “raised the colours” far higher than any plastic patriot with a pair of stepladders or political spiv with Union Jack socks could ever do. So, regardless of what happens tonight, lads: thanks. Job done.

Sports.title: Argentina star's wife labels Jude Bellingham 'useless' after new footage of slap

Tensions flared between Jude Bellingham and Argentina's Valentin Barco after the Three Lions were knocked out in the semi‑finals

Juareguy posted footage of the moment Bellingham appeared to slap Barco without provocation during England's World Cup semi‑final defeat to Argentina earlier this week.

‌



However, it has since emerged that Barco had antagonised England players earlier in the match. Tempers flared at full‑time when Bellingham confronted his opponent as the Chelsea‑bound star celebrated with his team‑mates.

The referee had to rush over to pull Barco away from the England players, though the former Brighton ace escaped any further punishment. Argentina came from 1-0 down to win 2-1 and book their place in Sunday's final against Spain (8pm).

Sports.title: FIFA reach decision on World Cup final intervention after 'dangerous' weather
Sports.content:
FIFA reach decision on World Cup final intervention after 'dangerous' weather

Spain and Argentina are set to play out the 2026 World Cup final on Sunday evening, despite concerns over 'dangerous' weather rolling in from Canada

View 2 Images Lionel Scaloni's nation stamped their place in the final with a 2-1 win over England (Image: Getty)

The World Cup final will proceed as planned at 8pm on Sunday evening at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. That's despite growing concerns over potentially 'dangerous' environmental conditions.

‌



Luis de la Fuente's Spain are set to play against Lionel Scaloni's Argentina in what should be an instant classic. However, smoke billowing from Canadian wildfires had brought speculation on whether or not the match would ultimately go ahead in New Jersey, or be moved elsewhere.

‌



Air quality was recorded as 'unhealthy for sensitive groups' this week - with NJ.gov identifying those groups as individuals suffering from asthma, lung disease or heart disease, along with older adults, children and infants.

‌



A health expert has also issued a stark warning that conditions could prove 'dangerous' for certain fans. In an interview with the Daily Mail, pulmonologist Dr Vin Gupta said: "It not only is going to be terrible, terrible air quality. It's hot, and that can cause an extreme amount of stress on the heart [for players].

"That is a very powerful and dangerous one-two punch to the human body. It's going to be critical to maintain core body temperatures as low as possible."

Despite such concerns, FIFA have no intention of altering either the timing or the venue of the World Cup final. Bloomberg has reported that a White House official confirmed that no major formal meetings are scheduled regarding the matter.

‌



However, informal talks regarding the decision have taken place between FIFA and Andrew Guiliani, who leads the White House's World Cup task force. A National Weather Service spokesperson, meanwhile, confirmed that personnel have been continuously deployed at the FIFA command centre in Miami and will keep monitoring conditions throughout the weekend.

View 2 Images The World Cup final takes place on Sunday (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

A National Weather Service spokesperson, meanwhile, confirmed that personnel have been continuously deployed at the FIFA command centre in Miami and will keep monitoring conditions throughout the weekend.

‌



It comes as Spain and Argentina stand prepared to clash at the MetLife Stadium, whatever the weather brings. Luis de la Fuente's side booked their place in Sunday's final with a commanding 2-0 victory over France, Mikel Oyarzabal slotting home from the penalty spot in the opening half before Pedro Porro sealed the result in the second.

Argentina, meanwhile, pulled off a stunning 2-1 triumph over England on Wednesday evening, the Three Lions crashing out of the tournament in brutal fashion. Anthony Gordon put his country ahead 55 minutes into the contest, only for Enzo Fernandez to level things up for Argentina with five minutes remaining.

Lautaro Martinez clinched victory for Argentina with a header at the back post two minutes into stoppage time, with Thomas Tuchel facing harsh criticism for his cautious approach after taking the lead.

Article continues below

Despite their semi-final exit from the competition, England's campaign in North America isn't quite over.

They will now take on France in a third-place play-off encounter at the Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, Florida, at 10pm on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate's private feelings on England job as 'dream role' window closes
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate's private feelings on England job as 'dream role' window closes

It has been two years since Gareth Southgate left the England job and those around him get a sense of how he feels following the Three Lions World Cup exit

View 2 Images Gareth Southgate led England for eight years and can boast a stellar record (Image: Bloomberg, Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Gareth Southgate's friends sense that he does feel undervalued after his spell in management, according to reports, as his absence from the game extends to two years.

‌



The former England boss has enjoyed a watching berth since leaving in the wake of the loss in the final of Euro 2024 - the second final he'd lost in the space of three years.

‌



Southgate though was the man to begin the Three Lions' renaissance when he led them to the semi-finals of the World Cup in 2018. Across the three tournaments that followed he would make two finals and a quarter-final before departing.

‌



During that tenure he did cop criticism for not being able to have the in-game impact that his elite counterparts did whilst some also cited favourable draws as key to his achievements.

The Telegraph reports that there is a sense among those close to him that his work doesn't get the appreciation it deserves. He helped unearth a new generation of players and, despite Thomas Tuchel being cited as a level up, the German has been unable to better his World Cup semi-final.

In fact several of the flaws that were associated with Southgate, such as a defensive approach and an inability to control games, are now being levelled at Tuchel after England blew their 1-0 lead over Argentina on Wednesday night.

‌



Southgate remains a man out of a managerial gig, but is by no means without things to occupy him as the 55-year-old enjoys several engagements away from football.

View 2 Images Gareth Southgate guided England to two finals - but came unstuck in both (Image: Hesham Elsherif/Anadolu via Getty Images)

There has been talk of him taking charge at Manchester United, the club he supported as a boy. Whilst that would be a dream job Southgate believes he needs to prove himself if he's to land an elite job and Michael Carrick's appointment may have closed that avenue.

‌



He was initially linked when Dan Ashworth, who worked with him at England, was in a senior role at Old Trafford. Ashworth has since been moved on but that hasn't stopped the speculation as and when the job becomes available.

Southgate's only club role has been with Middlesbrough and he's spoken about a desire to change the narrative having presided over the club's relegation.

Sports.title: More history at The Open! Fox enters golf's major '62 club'
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox followed Lucas Herbert and Sam Burns into the history books at The 154th Open, becoming the latest players to join an exclusive club with a '62 round' in men's major.

Herbert matched the lowest round in Open history with an eight-under 62 at Royal Birkdale, eight years on from Branden Grace becoming the first to manage it - at the same venue - during the third round of the 2017 contest.

The Australian threatened to post an even lower total when he was nine under with two holes to play, including a par-five reachable in two, but carded a par-bogey finish to register only the sixth 62 in men's majors.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lucas Herbert missed a short putt on the 18th green and was denied the chance to set a new The Open scoring record

Herbert's 62 was matched by Burns during an extraordinary day, with the American holing out from the greenside bunker at the par-four last to close a three-birdie finish to his second-round 62.

Burns and Herbert's efforts came six days after Haeran Ryu smashed the major record with a third-round 60 during her victory at the Amundi Evian Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Haeran Ryu makes history after shooting the lowest-ever round in a men's or women's major at the Amundi Evian Championship

Further history was made a day later as Fox charged up the leaderboard during the third round, mixing nine birdies with a lone bogey to set the early clubhouse lead, marking the first time ever that three players posted a '62 round' in the same week of a major

Who has made a '62 round' in a major and how have they done it? Here's a closer look at every player to post a record-equalling men's major score so far…

Branden Grace, The Open, 2017 (R3)

There had previously been 31 rounds of 63 in men's major championship history, but South African Grace became the first male to go lower after carding eight birdies in a bogey-free round at Royal Birkdale.

He posted five birdies in a front-nine 29 and followed another at the 14th with back-to-back gains from the 16th, with a two-putt par at the last enough to set the new benchmark in the men's game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of Branden Grace's historic round as he became the first man to shoot 62 at a major

Rickie Fowler, US Open, 2023 (R1)

Fowler became the first player to card a '62 round' at a US Open, mixing 10 birdies with two bogeys to move to eight under in benign conditions on the par-70 layout at Los Angeles Country Club.

Fowler posted three birdies in a five-hole stretch from the 12th and cancelled out a bogey at the 17th with a four-birdie run, then picked up shots at the sixth and eighth before two-putting from 60 feet for a closing par.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at the highlights from Rickie Fowler's stunning eight-under round of 62 that set a new US Open record

Xander Schauffele, US Open, 2023 (R1)

Just hours after Fowler made US Open history, Schauffele followed suit at the same venue after carding eight birdies in a bogey-free start to his bid for a maiden major title.

Schauffele made a 40-footer on his opening hole and posted three birdies in his first five, with five more after the turn - including a 60-footer from the fringe at the fifth - lifting him to eight under.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the opening day of the 2023 US Open, where Xander Schauffele also made a record-breaking start

Xander Schauffele, PGA Championship, 2024 (R1)

Schauffele carded nine birdies during a stunning bogey-free opening round at Valhalla Golf Club, seeing him record the first '62 round' in the PGA Championship and just the fourth ever in a men's major.

He became the first player to card multiple rounds of 62 in major history, with an opening round of nine under also equalling the lowest score - relative to par - ever in a men's major, with Schauffele two-putting from 30 feet on his final hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Xander Schauffele became the first player in PGA Championship history to card a round of 62 with a sensational performance at Valhalla

Shane Lowry, PGA Championship, 2024 (R3)

Lowry was eight strokes off the halfway lead but produced a stunning nine-under 62, two days on from Schauffele, carding nine birdies in a bogey-free round and missed a chance on the final hole preventing the first '61 round' in a men's major.

He raced to the turn in 29 and posted back-to-back birdies from the 13th, with Lowry adding another at the 17th before missing a 12-foot birdie chance at the last for the outright record.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch every birdie from Shane Lowry's record equalling men's major round as he shot a nine-under-par 62 at Valhalla

Lucas Herbert, The Open, 2026 (R2)

Herbert had equalled the lowest front-nine in major history as he raced to the turn in 28, with a 40-footer at the seventh among six birdies on the front nine, with the Australian adding back-to-back gains from the 11th to get to eight under.

A sub-60 round was not out of the question when he birdied the 16th and found the fairway off the tee at the par-five next, but Herbert missed a 10-footer for birdie before agonisingly squandering a putt from five feet to save par at the last.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lucas Herbert reached the turn in 28 during his second round at The Open, equalling the lowest front nine in men's major history

Sam Burns, The Open, 2026 (R2)

Burns was playing two groups behind Herbert and reached the turn in 32, with the American starting his back nine with successive birdies and adding another from tap-in range at the 13th.

He picked up a shot at the 16th and rolled in from 20 feet to birdie the 17th, then delighted record-breaking Open crowds by holing from the greenside bunker to birdie the par-four last and add his own place in history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Burns holed out from the bunker at 18 for a closing birdie to match Herbert's eight-under 62 and equal the men's major record

Ryan Fox, The Open, 2026 (R3)

Fox followed three birdies in the first five holes by holing from 55 feet for another at the par-four sixth, with the New Zealander picking up a shot at the eighth to reach the turn in 29 and then starting his back nine with a birdie.

He cancelled out a bogey at the 13th by taking advantage of the par-five next and posting back-to-back birdies from the 16th, leaving him searching for a final-hole birdie for outright history, with a two-putt par at the last enough to add him into the '62 club'.

Image: Ryan Fox equalled major history with a third-round 62 at The 154th Open

The lowest round at The Masters is a 63, posted by Nick Price in 1986 and Greg Norman during the opening round in 1996, while there have been numerous 63 rounds in each of the PGA Championship, US Open and The Open.

The lowest round on the PGA Tour is a 58, posted by Jim Furyk at the 2016 Travelers Championship, while the record on the DP World Tour is Oliver Fisher's 59 at the 2018 Portugal Masters.

Sports.title: Hamilton crashes out as Antonelli sets pace in final Belgium practice
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari crew face a race against time to repair his car for Belgian Grand Prix Qualifying after he crashed at the end of final practice, in a session topped again by Mercedes' title-leading Kimi Antonelli.

​Fifth-fastest Hamilton was on a quick lap in the closing moments of the final session before Qualifying at 3pm this afternoon when he went wide across the gravel at Turn 13 and his car's right rear wheel had a glancing blow against the barrier.

It was a near mirror image of Pierre Gasly's crash at the same corner on Friday for Alpine.

"I've destroyed the car mate," said Hamilton to his race engineer over team radio.

"I'm sorry."

With sufficient damage to the SF-26's right rear preventing the Briton from driving it back to the pit lane, Hamilton soon stopped on track and was then seen inspecting the damage himself once climbing out of the cockpit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports’ Karun Chandhok is at the SkyPad analysing how Lewis Hamilton ended up crashing in FP3 and comparing it to a very similar crash involving Pierre Gasly during FP2 on Friday.

Antonelli will go into Qualifying as the clear favourite for pole position after he topped the timesheet for the second second running at a sun-kissed Spa.

Despite seeing his once comfortable title lead cut to 25 points over recent events, Antonelli has continued to show supreme pace relative to his rivals and that has hitherto continued around one of F1's most legendary and challenging circuits.

He was immediately a full 0.7s faster than anyone else on his first lap of the session mid-way through the hour, although his final gap over second-placed Lando Norris and third-placed Max Verstappen finished at just 0.1s after Antonelli did not improve on the final soft-tyre runs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli goes fastest by a huge margin during the final practice session at the Belgian GP

George Russell finished 0.3s back on his Mercedes team-mate in fourth ahead of the Ferrari pair of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton has had a clear pace edge on British GP victor Leclerc so far this weekend and was nearly 0.4s faster than his team-mate in final practice.

Norris was the lead McLaren driver in second place but he will carry a 10-place grid penalty into Qualifying owing to engine changes. His team-mate Oscar Piastri will therefore effectively carry the Woking team's challenge, but the Australian finished final practice almost 0.8s off the pace in seventh place.

Audi enjoyed a promising session as Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto finished eighth and ninth respectively ahead of Isack Hadjar in the second Red Bull.

Hadjar already knows he will start Sunday's race from the back of the grid owing to penalties for multiple changes of power-unit parts, with the Frenchman's P3 session briefly interrupted by an issue which stopped his RB22 in the pit lane after leaving the garage.

Sports.title: Ruthless All Blacks prove too strong for Ireland at Eden Park
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - New Zealand 40-21 Ireland: Ruthless All Blacks prove too strong for off-colour visitors at Eden Park

New Zealand secured a bonus-point Nations Championship win over Ireland at Eden Park on Saturday

A ruthless All Blacks display ensured they will end their home block of rugby's inaugural Nations Championship with three wins from three, after emphatically beating Ireland 40-21 at Eden Park.

With Ireland shorn of 12 players through injury, their performance left a lot to be desired, with their attack particularly poor and lacking in zip or threat.

Defensively Andy Farrell's side also conceded six tries, with lock Patrick Tuipulotu, No 8 Ardie Savea, wing Will Jordan, hooker Asafo Aumua, full-back Damian McKenzie and replacement Anton Lienert-Brown all crossing for New Zealand, who were fortunate not to lose flanker Luke Jacobson to a first-half red card for a dangerous clearout.

Ireland scored three tries through No 8 Jack Conan, lock Joe McCarthy and full-back Hugo Keenan, narrowing to 14-7 late in the first half, and within 14 points twice in the second, but they couldn't grab a fourth score to at least leave with a bonus-point.

New Zealand 40-21 Ireland - Score summary New Zealand - Tries: Tuipulotu (15), Savea (22), Jordan (35), Aumua (39), McKenzie (56), Lienert-Brown (79). Cons: Love (15,23,36,40,57). Ireland - Tries: Conan (33), McCarthy (45), Keenan (63). Cons: Prendergast (34,45,64).

Instead, Ireland's errors - plentiful in the contest - were preyed upon and exposed in a disappointing finish to the visitors' season.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Dave Rennie's selections bore early fruit as the repositioned Tupou Vaa'i made a blistering start at blindside flanker and the new second row of Tuipulotu and Josh Lord combined for the first try ​on 15 minutes.

A strong carry by Vaa'i on the right shredded Ireland's defence, and Tuipulotu latched ⁠onto a pass from Lord to thunder over the line.

Lock Patrick Tuipulotu dived over for the first try of the contest in the 15th minute

Less than ⁠10 minutes later, New Zealand doubled the lead, with Savea breaking from the back of a scrum near the try-line past poor Irish defence for their second.

All Blacks momentum stalled when loose ‌forward Jacobson earned a yellow card and off-field review for a clean-out to the head of a prone Josh van Der Flier with a tucked arm. To huge surprise, the review did not bring an upgraded red card for the incident.

All Blacks captain Ardie Savea crashed over for their second try past poor Irish defence

Ireland rallied through their forwards and rumbled over the line, with a charging Conan crashing over from two metres out, taking a fizzed pass out of a ‌ruck from scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park.

Ireland's joy turned to despair two minutes later as Jordan scooped up an errant pass inside the Irish 22 from the restart and cantered over for his sixth try of the season - Stuart McCloskey and Sam Prendergast seeming to cross wires.

Just after Ireland got within seven point, Will Jordan gladly accepted a gift of a try from the restart

Aumua made it four tries for the hosts, when a TMO review showed he planted the ball on the chalk near the right post on the cusp of half-time.

Lock McCarthy delivered the spark Ireland badly ⁠needed early in the second half, doing well to ground over the line under the posts, thanks in ​part to a helpful latch by captain Dan Sheehan.

Again, the All Blacks hit back ​quickly with pace and unrelenting pressure.

With quick hands shifting the ball to the left, fly-half Ruben Love ​was stopped a foot from the line but fullback McKenzie scooped up the recycled ball and popped it ⁠over.

Ireland's attack proved poor on the day, lacking zip and threat and filled with errors

Ireland again closed within two converted tries after the hour-mark, with Keenan crossing unmarked at the left corner following another forwards-led assault.

The All Blacks had the last reply, though, as a Jordan offload found Lienert-Brown, who finished off Ireland with a sixth ⁠try in the final minute.

Farrell laments Ireland's 'inaccuracy' and 'lack of flow'

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell said post-match:

"Inaccurate is the word. Our continuity, we just weren't flowing for all sorts of reasons, whether that be discipline, spilt ball, throwing the ball into touch etc.

"The character and fight is there for all to see, and we saw that against Australia as well.

"But you cannot make so many errors against a quality side like New Zealand.

"When injuries occur, it's someone else's opportunity. It's priceless for us with what's coming over the next 15 months."

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell lamented his side's errors and poor attack

McKenzie: Our most physical Test of summer - awesome to come out with tough win

Player of the match Damian McKenzie said post-match:

"A tough Test match. Ireland came out strong, and we knew we had to start well.

"We had to keep at our work, and the second half was still a grind. The Irish boys are a tough side.

"We had to work really hard for our points in the second half. Awesome to come away with a tough Test win.

"These Tests get more physical every week."

Sports.title: Joshua vs Itauma is 'perfect story' for Nigeria fight, says promoter
Sports.content:
A "blockbuster fight" between Anthony Joshua and Moses Itauma in Nigeria would create more global interest than Muhammad Ali’s 'Rumble in the Jungle', says promoter Dr Ezekiel Adamu.

The British heavyweight stars currently have their own plans as Joshua returns against Kristian Prenga later this month before an expected all-British battle with Tyson Fury, while Itauma faces Filip Hrgovic on August 29.

But Adamu believes Joshua and Itauma, who both have Nigerian heritage, could surpass Ali's legendary fight with George Foreman in Zaire [former name of DR Congo], if they both shared the ring in Nigeria.

"It's a global fight. We'll get some huge numbers when it comes to viewership," Adamu told Sky Sports.

"When you think about Africa as a whole, we have about 1.4 billion people in Africa. And then 70 to 75 per cent of that population between the ages of 15 to 30 or thereabouts. Having those eyeballs on it as well too is major.

"And then both of them are global stars. So it's a perfect story in Africa, where they come from, from their roots.

"It's one fight that will actually top the Rumble in the Jungle we've been talking about for about 50 years.

"So I'd like to make that fight happen here."

Joshua is a two-time world champion who is on a collision course with long-term rival Fury as he enters the final chapter of his career, whereas the unbeaten Itauma has blazed a trail towards a world title with 14 straight wins.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moses Itauma is taking a step up in class when he faces Croatian Filip Hrgovic in August

But Adamu is hopeful Joshua would be interested in a fight with his expected successor on African soil.

"AJ has made it clear he wants to become undisputed again, so he's going to go on and keep fighting after this fight with Fury," said Adamu.

"He's got the appetite to keep fighting.

"We are also looking at bringing big fights here to Nigeria as well. So the one wish I would have at some point before his career ends, would be to have AJ vs Moses Itauma here in Nigeria.

"Both Nigerians on Nigerian soil, that would really be a blockbuster fight."

Sports.title: Bint Archange features in the Super Sprint at Newbury
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Saturday with flat action from Doncaster, Newbury and Ripon, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.37 Newbury - Bint Archange and Sky Secret fancied for calvary charge

A typically open renewal of this 25-runner Weatherbys Super Sprint sees Bint Archange among the market principals.

Richard Hughes has always held his charge in the highest regard, and he justified his reputation when landing the Listed Dragon Stakes at Sandown earlier this month. His trainer immediately pinpointed this as a likely target, and she could hit the frame with stall 20 a big plus.

Sky Secret was given a positive mention by trainer Clive Cox this week and he could be the main danger. P J McDonald takes the ride and given he wandered a little under pressure when winning at Leicester, there should be plenty more to come.

The pick of Richard Spencer's pair looks to be Etienne who finished a narrow second behind Weekend Roar at Newmarket and he could play a part if settling early on.

Debut winner Angels Lane and the experienced Vollering complete a long list of alternatives.

3.02 Newbury - Symbol Of Honour and Soldier's Tree feature

A tightly knit field of seven have assembled for this Group Three Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes at 3.02pm.

The James Owen-trained Soldier's Tree steps into Group company for the first time having shown excellent placed form in handicaps this summer. Third in the Wokingham on his last outing was an great run, and he this lightly raced individual may be competitive in this grade.

Symbol Of Honour, winner of the Sandy Lane last season, has failed to reach those heights since but was not beaten far when third at Newcastle and must be feared if in similar mood.

Binhareer is another with solid claims after a fair run at Royal Ascot, while Ed Walker's Noble Champion is top-rated on 112.

1.55 Newbury - Persica and Oceans Four headline six runners

A select field of six goes to post for this opening Listed Steventon Stakes where Persica looks to have obvious claims.

Richard Hannon's five-year-old is a dual Group Three winner and he was just denied when second in the Diomed Stakes at Epsom in June. Beaten the last twice, he continues to hold his form though and merits respect under Sean Levey.

Oceans Four produced a career-best when finishing fourth in the Hampton Court Stakes at Royal Ascot last month and first-time cheekpieces may eke out further improvement.

Godolphin pair Al Zanati and Arabian Light are worth closer inspection.

But how much will these additions’ financial success, if not universal popularity, embolden Fifa to take the same approach at their other tournaments? Will we see hydration breaks at next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil, for example, or the 2030 men’s edition? If tomorrow’s half-time show – rumoured to widen the break to 30 minutes – is a hit, do we see the same at the Bernabéu in four years’ time? And what about ticket prices? 40m ago 09.28 EDT A (rare) comment leaping to Thomas Tuchel’s defence BTL … Some points re. England semi final: 1. England cannot hold the ball. None of the players seem capable of doing so. It's always been thus, certainly since 66. We rely on booting it up the pitch and hoping we're fast enough to catch up. This leads to players tiring at the end of matches and, if we're lucky enough, tiring at the end of tournaments. 2. Tuchel had to bring on defenders because he could see they'd run out of fuel. 3. If you watch and listen carefully, you can see he's imploring them to keep the ball and advance forward. He was going so from the side of the pitch and during the hydration break. The players ignored him. Perhaps they were too knackered to follow the orders, perhaps, through Bellingham, he'd lost the dressing room. 4. He could've replaced the front with new attackers by Argentina would've adjusted to attack on the break. With England's flawed defenders Messi would've cut through them. So, stop haranguing Tuchel. He did the best with what he had - ordinary defenders and midfield, and strikers that disappeared. Yes, he could've put a fresh attack on but I suspect he would have had to take them off again at 75-80 mins when he had seen Argentina cut through then on the counter. If we're serious about winning something, the coach needs more time with the players, club power needs to be reduced, and youth players need better training on keeping the ball, playing with intelligence and coaching to stay calm and not hoof the ball up the field. Sports.title: Football Daily | France v England in the third-place playoff: the game nobody wants to play
Sports.content:
THE FUN FINAL?

Saturday’s rebranded “bronze final” between France and England in Miami might feel like a modern, Gianni-coded exercise in squeezing the product dry, but the third-place playoff is a staple of World Cup history, even if it remains the game nobody wants to play in. The very first TPPO came in 1934, Germany defeating Austria 3-2 in a match engulfed in murky, menacing geopolitics. Thankfully, the fixture quickly became a more knockabout affair – Brazil swaggered on to the world stage by beating Sweden 4-2 in 1938, and France put six past West Germany in a nine-goal feast of football 20 years later. Just Fontaine scored four that day, later to be joined by Thomas Müller, Davor Suker and Toto Schillaci in using the fixture to pad their Golden Boot stats – a tactic Kylian Mbappé might want to try against a punch-drunk England side and pip Lionel Messi to another personal accolade as a result.

Yes, the third-place playoff can have a hungover, world-weary vibe, but it can also be a lot of fun. The goals-per-game average is higher than in the final, and the TPPO has never gone to penalties. But does the result matter? It depends who you ask. Back in 1982, France lost an all-time classic semi-final on penalties to West Germany, and were extremely laissez-faire against Poland just two days later. “Our hearts were elsewhere,” Alain Giresse recalled 40 years on. “We had pulled the plug.” On the other hand, Poland’s 3-2 victory meant they matched their best-ever performance, having also won the TPPO against Brazil in 1970. Plenty of other teams have secured a new personal best via this fixture, including Austria, Chile, Portugal, Turkey and Belgium, whose 2-0 triumph over a checked-out England sealed third place in 2018, and a rousing civic reception when the squad returned home.

Even if no player or team truly enjoys this game, England still like it less than most. Their two previous appearances have ended in defeat – against Italy in 1990, and the aforementioned Belgium clash in 2018. Not even Carlo Ancelotti would raise an eyebrow if England come up short again on Saturday, against an all-star France attack eager to take out their frustration on anyone in their path. But if England can be a little more Azteca, a little less Atlanta, then their best men’s World Cup performance since 1966 is in reach. So dig Kobbie Mainoo out of storage, fire up Wonderwall and get in the mood. What do you reckon, Thomas Tuchel? “None of our players and none of the French players want to play this match.” Ah. Still, would victory at least earn Tuchel some breathing room, a shiny bronze medal to point at as hacks keep banging on about the Argentina game? The short, and indeed long answer is no. But there are just two bites left at this summer-long buffet of football, so we’re going to watch it anyway.
